text:
maria: Powershell autocomplete for redwoodctl stopped loading after I updated to 0.9.2. tab completion just does nothing. anyone seen this?

sam: hm haven't hit it on mac, are you on Windows?

maria: yeah Windows 11 + PowerShell 7.3. Did the usual: 
```
redwoodctl completion --shell powershell | Out-File -FilePath $profile -Append
. $profile
```
but nothing shows up for commands like `redwoodctl config` or `redwoodctl auth`.

jordan: two quick checks: is execution policy blocking the profile? `Get-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser`

maria: it was Restricted. I did `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser` and restarted terminal, still no dice.

sam: any errors when you dot-source the profile? run `. $profile` and then `Get-Module -ListAvailable | Where-Object Name -match 'redwood'`

maria: `Get-Module` shows nothing. The completion script output looks tiny: `# redwoodctl powershell completion v0.9.2` then nothing else.

jordan: oh, that sounds like the wrapper emitted a bash-style script by mistake on windows. can you run `redwoodctl completion --shell powershell --debug` and paste the header output?

maria: pasted:
```
DEBUG: detected shell=unknown
#compdef redwoodctl
_complete_redwoodctl() { ... }
```
so it's actually printing an zsh/fish style script.

oliver: ack. looks like our completion generator mis-detected shell on Win when TERM isn't set. repro steps: start pwsh with NO_COLOR and empty TERM, run command -> outputs generic POSIX script.

maria: thanks. separate but related: profile switching also weird. I have 2 profiles (personal, work). `redwoodctl auth login --profile work` returns success, but `redwoodctl whoami` still shows personal unless I restart terminal. is that expected?

sam: no, should be immediate. how are you switching profiles typically? `redwoodctl config use-profile work` or setting `REDWOOD_PROFILE` env var?

maria: i do `redwoodctl auth login --profile work` only. i assumed it becomes current.

jordan: auth login creates a token in `%APPDATA%/redwoodctl/credentials` under profile name but doesn't change the active profile. `config use-profile` is the explicit switch. we probably need clearer UX or auto-switch flag.

oliver: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1245 — title "powershell completion detects wrong shell on windows + auth login doesn't set active profile" :eyes:

maria: repro steps for the profile problem for the issue:
1) `redwoodctl auth login --profile work`
2) run `redwoodctl whoami` -> returns personal user
3) `redwoodctl config use-profile work` -> whoami shows work user
4) restart terminal -> work user shown even without explicit `use-profile` after login

sam: that suggests `auth login` writes creds but doesn't update the in-memory active config until process restart or explicit `use-profile`. we should either update active config on login or warn in docs.

jordan: devex note: local serve also picks up the wrong profile in some flows. `redwoodctl serve --local` prefers `$REDWOOD_PROFILE` -> `config.active` -> fallback to default. if you rely on `auth login` to switch, you'll be surprised.

maria: workaround for now: `redwoodctl config use-profile work && start pwsh` then `redwoodctl serve --local`.

oliver: pulled a quick patch to completion detection (PR #1289) to prefer explicit `--shell` if provided and fallback to windows defaults. also adding a small note to `auth login` output: "note: run `redwoodctl config use-profile <name>` to make this active".

maria: thanks! any way to auto-install completion into current profile via a flag?

sam: we can add `--install` to write and dot-source, but on Windows we'd also need to check execution policy. maybe `redwoodctl completion --shell powershell --install` would be fine with a user prompt.

jordan: added to the issue as feature request.

maria: last oddity — `redwoodctl --debug whoami` prints token file path, which helped. sample:
```
DEBUG: credentials path=C:\Users\maria\AppData\Roaming\redwoodctl\credentials
profile=personal
token_expires=2026-05-01T12:34:56Z
```
helpful for triage.

oliver: devex-bot: tagged @devex to triage. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all, workaround works. i'll test the PR when it's up. :rocket:
